title: Pancreatic Cancer Pill Hailed as Biggest Breakthrough in Decades
summary: Daraxonrasib, a new pill for advanced pancreatic cancer that has metastasized, showed tumors stopped growing in 90% of trial patients and 76.6% survived after one year compared to typical 40–45% with chemotherapy. Doctors cautioned the pill is not yet a cure and long-term outcomes remain unknown.
takeaways: 90% of 61 trial patients had tumor growth halted
60% had tumors shrink or disappear; ~8% (1 in 12) became cancer-undetectable
76.6% one-year survival versus typical 40–45% with chemotherapy alone
Pancreatic cancer normally kills 50% within three months when metastasized
Longer studies planned; cure status unknown
